lessons.title: (a) Nazra Quran: Para 21 to Para 30
lessons.notes_html:
Introduction to the Holy Quran

The Holy Quran is the last revealed Book of Allah Almighty. It was revealed to the last Prophet, Hazrat Muhammad ﷺ, gradually over a period of twenty-three (23) years. It has thirty (30) Paras and one hundred and fourteen (114) Surahs. The purpose of its revelation is to show mankind such a way of living that, by acting upon it, they can lead a life of honour and success in this world and in the Hereafter. Memorizing the Holy Quran is a great act of worship, and there is great reward in reciting it: according to the saying of the Holy Prophet ﷺ, ten virtues are received for reciting every single letter of the Holy Quran.

Aims of this Chapter

  • Students should be able to read the Holy Quran correctly, with proper accent, in Salah and in daily life.
  • They should memorize a part of it and read the translation of a part of it.
  • Love for pondering over the Quran, acting upon it and preaching it should be created in them.

(a) Nazra Quran: Para 21 to Para 30 (Ten Paras)

In this class, ten Paras of the Holy Quran (from Para 21 to Para 30) will be read as Nazra with Tajweed. Their names are:

  • Para 21: أُتْلُ مَا أُوحِيَ (Utlu Ma Uhiya)
  • Para 22: وَمَنْ يَقْنُتْ (Wa Manyaqnut)
  • Para 23: وَمَالِيَ (Wa Maliya)
  • Para 24: فَمَنِ اظْلَمُ (Famaniz Zalam)
  • Para 25: إِلَيْهِ يُرَدُّ (Ilaihi Yuraddu)
  • Para 26: حم (Ha Meem)
  • Para 27: قَالَ فَمَا خَطْبُكُمْ (Qala Fama Khatbukum)
  • Para 28: قَدْ سَمِعَ اللهُ (Qad Sami'ullah)
  • Para 29: تَبَارَكَ الَّذِي (Tabarakallazi)
  • Para 30: عَمَّ يَتَسَاءَلُونَ (Amma Yatasa'aloon)

Important Points about Nazra

  • An oral examination of the Nazra and Hifz portions is taken in the mid-term and annual examinations, and the marks obtained are included in the result sheet.
  • Out of the total 100 marks of Islamiat, 40 marks are fixed for Nazra, and passing in Nazra Quran is compulsory for passing in Islamiat.
  • Note: This is an oral unit of the book; it has no written exercise. These notes and MCQs are made from the textbook's own pages of this chapter.

mcqs.q: In Class 8, which Paras of the Holy Quran are read as Nazra?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Para 21 to Para 30. In Class 8, ten Paras — from Para 21 to Para 30 — are read as Nazra with Tajweed, as the textbook's chapter states.

mcqs.q: What is the name of Para 21?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Utlu Ma Uhiya (أُتْلُ مَا أُوحِيَ). It is the opening words of Para 21, the first Para of the Class 8 Nazra portion.

mcqs.q: What is the name of Para 29?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Tabarakallazi (تَبَارَكَ الَّذِي). Para 29 begins with these words; the solved exercise of the book also names it among the ten Paras.

mcqs.q: What is the name of the last Para, Para 30?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Amma Yatasa'aloon (عَمَّ يَتَسَاءَلُونَ). Para 30, the last Para of the Holy Quran, begins with Surah An-Naba, whose opening words give the Para its name.

mcqs.q: What is the name of Para 25?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Ilaihi Yuraddu (إِلَيْهِ يُرَدُّ). It is the name of Para 25 in the list of ten Paras prescribed for Class 8.

mcqs.q: How many Paras and Surahs are there in the Holy Quran?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 30 Paras and 114 Surahs. The textbook's introduction states that the Holy Quran has thirty Paras and one hundred and fourteen Surahs.

mcqs.q: Over how many years was the Holy Quran revealed to the Holy Prophet ﷺ?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 23 years. The Quran was revealed to the last Prophet Hazrat Muhammad ﷺ gradually, little by little, over twenty-three years.

mcqs.q: According to the Hadith, how many virtues are received for reciting one letter of the Holy Quran?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is ten virtues. The textbook quotes the saying of the Holy Prophet ﷺ that ten virtues are received for every single letter of the Holy Quran recited.

mcqs.q: How many marks out of the 100 marks of Islamiat are fixed for Nazra Quran?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 40 marks. The chapter states that out of the total 100 marks of Islamiat, 40 marks are for Nazra, and passing in Nazra is compulsory for passing the subject.

mcqs.q: What is the name of Para 28?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Qad Sami'ullah (قَدْ سَمِعَ اللهُ). Para 28 begins with Surah Al-Mujadila, and its opening words are the name of the Para.

lessons.title: (b) Hifz Quran: Three Surahs
lessons.notes_html:
(b) Hifz Quran: Three Surahs

In this class, three Surahs are to be memorized:

  • Surah Al-Adiyat (11 verses): In this Surah, an oath is taken by the running war horses, and it is told that man is very ungrateful to his Lord, he is intense in the love of wealth, and on the Day when those in the graves are raised and the secrets of the chests are made known, Allah Almighty knows everything.
  • Surah At-Takathur (8 verses): The greed for more and more made man heedless, until he reached the graves. On the Day of Judgement, he will surely be questioned about the blessings.
  • Surah Al-Humazah (9 verses): Woe to every slanderer and backbiter who gathers wealth and counts it again and again, thinking that his wealth will make him live forever. Such a person will be thrown into Al-Hutamah, which is the kindled Fire of Allah.

Note: This is an oral (memorization) part of the book and has no written exercise; these notes and MCQs are made from the textbook's own pages of this chapter.

mcqs.q: Which of the following Surahs is included in the Class 8 Hifz portion?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Surah Al-Adiyat. The three Surahs prescribed for memorization in Class 8 are Surah Al-Adiyat, Surah At-Takathur and Surah Al-Humazah.

mcqs.q: How many verses are there in Surah Al-Adiyat?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 11 verses. Surah Al-Adiyat, one of the three Hifz Surahs, has eleven verses, as stated in the textbook.

mcqs.q: How many verses are there in Surah At-Takathur?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 8 verses. Surah At-Takathur has eight verses and warns that greed for more makes man heedless until he reaches the graves.

mcqs.q: How many verses are there in Surah Al-Humazah?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 9 verses. Surah Al-Humazah has nine verses and condemns the slanderer and backbiter who hoards wealth.

mcqs.q: In Surah Al-Adiyat, an oath is taken by which of the following?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is running war horses. The Surah opens with an oath by the panting war horses that charge into battle, as the textbook explains.

mcqs.q: According to Surah At-Takathur, about what will man surely be questioned on the Day of Judgement?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the blessings given to him. The Surah ends by saying that on that Day people will surely be asked about the blessings they enjoyed in the world.

mcqs.q: Surah Al-Humazah gives a warning of woe to whom?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the slanderer and backbiter. The Surah begins: woe to every person who finds faults in others and speaks ill of them behind their backs.

mcqs.q: In Surah Al-Humazah, what does the wealthy misguided person think about his wealth?
options: That it will make him live forever
That it will be taken away soon
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that it will make him live forever. The Surah says he gathers wealth and keeps counting it, imagining that his wealth will make him immortal.

mcqs.q: What is Al-Hutamah, mentioned in Surah Al-Humazah?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the kindled Fire of Allah. The Surah says the backbiter will be thrown into Al-Hutamah, and explains that it is the fire of Allah, set ablaze.

mcqs.q: According to Surah Al-Adiyat, what is man's attitude towards his Lord mentioned in the Surah?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that he is very ungrateful. The Surah states that indeed man is, to his Lord, ungrateful, despite the countless blessings he receives.

lessons.title: (c) Hifz and Translation: Surah Al-Inshirah and Ayat-ul-Kursi
lessons.notes_html:
(c) Hifz and Translation: Surah Al-Inshirah

This Surah (8 verses) is to be memorized along with its translation. Its important points:

  • Allah Almighty opened the chest of the Holy Prophet ﷺ and removed from him his burden, which had weighed down his back.
  • Allah Almighty raised the fame of the Prophet ﷺ high: "وَرَفَعْنَا لَكَ ذِكْرَكَ" — Translation: "And We raised your praise high for you."
  • Surely, with hardship comes ease — this point is repeated twice in the Surah.
  • So when you are free (from your work), strive hard in worship, and turn your attention towards your Lord alone.

Ayat-ul-Kursi (Memorization with Translation)

Ayat-ul-Kursi is verse number 255 of Surah Al-Baqarah, and it is also to be memorized with its translation. Its important points:

  • There is no god worthy of worship except Allah; He is Ever-Living and the Sustainer of all.
  • Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him; whatever is in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him.
  • No one can intercede with Him except by His permission.
  • He knows everything, and the creation cannot encompass anything of His knowledge except what He wills.
  • His Kursi (kingdom) extends over the heavens and the earth, and guarding them does not tire Him; He is the Most High, the Most Great.

Summary of the Lesson

  • Ten Paras (21 to 30) of the Holy Quran must be read as Nazra.
  • Surah Al-Adiyat, Surah At-Takathur and Surah Al-Humazah must be memorized.
  • Surah Al-Inshirah and Ayat-ul-Kursi must be memorized along with translation.

Note: This is an oral unit of the book; it has no written exercise. These notes and MCQs are made from the textbook's own pages of this chapter.

mcqs.q: How many verses are there in Surah Al-Inshirah?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 8 verses. Surah Al-Inshirah, which is memorized with translation in Class 8, consists of eight verses.

mcqs.q: What is the translation of "وَرَفَعْنَا لَكَ ذِكْرَكَ"?
options: And We raised your praise high for you
And We sent you as a mercy
mcqs.why: The correct answer is "And We raised your praise high for you." This is the translation given in the book's own solved exercise for this verse of Surah Al-Inshirah.

mcqs.q: Which point is repeated twice in Surah Al-Inshirah?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is "with hardship comes ease." The textbook notes that this comforting point — surely with hardship there is ease — is repeated twice in the Surah.

mcqs.q: According to Surah Al-Inshirah, what should a person do when he is free from his work?
options: Strive hard in worship and turn to his Lord
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to strive hard in worship and turn to his Lord. The Surah ends with this instruction: when you are free, work hard in worship and direct your longing to your Lord alone.

mcqs.q: Ayat-ul-Kursi is verse 255 of which Surah?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Surah Al-Baqarah. Ayat-ul-Kursi is the 255th verse of Surah Al-Baqarah and is memorized with translation in this class.

mcqs.q: According to Ayat-ul-Kursi, what never overtakes Allah Almighty?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is drowsiness and sleep. The verse says: neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him — He is Ever-Living and always sustaining His creation.

mcqs.q: Who can intercede with Allah, according to Ayat-ul-Kursi?
options: No one except by His permission
mcqs.why: The correct answer is no one except by His permission. The verse makes clear that no one can intercede before Allah unless He permits it.

mcqs.q: What does the Kursi of Allah extend over, according to Ayat-ul-Kursi?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the heavens and the earth. The verse says His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth, showing the vastness of His kingdom.

mcqs.q: According to Ayat-ul-Kursi, guarding the heavens and the earth is for Allah:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is not tiring at all. The verse says that preserving the heavens and the earth does not weary Him, for He is the Most High, the Most Great.

mcqs.q: In Surah Al-Inshirah, Allah says He removed from the Holy Prophet ﷺ:
options: His burden that weighed down his back
mcqs.why: The correct answer is his burden that weighed down his back. The Surah reminds the Prophet ﷺ that Allah opened his chest and lifted the heavy burden from him.

lessons.title: Belief in the Hereafter (Aqeedah-e-Aakhirat)
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning of Aqeedah and the Hereafter

The literal meaning of Aqeedah is to hold firm belief in something. The Hereafter means the life after death. Belief in the Hereafter means having complete faith in the life that is to come after this world. It is one of the fundamental beliefs of Islam, and all the Prophets (AS) taught this belief.

Importance of the Belief

  • The Holy Quran says: وَبِالْآخِرَةِ هُمْ يُوقِنُونَ (Al-Baqarah: 4) — "They believe in the Hereafter." Faith in the Hereafter is the attribute of the guided and successful people.
  • Allah Almighty will destroy this world and all its things; then every person's deeds will be presented before the court of Allah Almighty.
  • On the Day of Judgement, the good and bad deeds of all human beings will be weighed, and reward and punishment will be given accordingly.
  • Paradise is the place of blessings and Hell is the place of punishment; those who are forgiven will enter Paradise.
  • The life of the Hereafter will be eternal, not temporary, and every person will be questioned about his responsibilities.

Effects on Human Character

  • Love for good and hatred for evil: when a Muslim believes that every deed of his is being recorded and he will be rewarded or punished on the Day of Judgement, he begins to love good and hate evil, and becomes a useful and righteous member of society.
  • Belief in the Hereafter makes a person a fully responsible person and gives him the sense of his own responsibility.
  • It makes a person generous (not miserly) and produces patience and tolerance in him instead of anger.
  • The believer has faith that performing his duty will bring reward in the Hereafter.

mcqs.q: What is the literal meaning of the word Aqeedah?
options: To hold firm belief in something
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to hold firm belief in something. The book's solved exercise explains that Aqeedah literally means having firm belief — belief, not doubt.

mcqs.q: What is meant by belief in the Hereafter?
options: Belief in this worldly life only
Complete faith in the life that is to come after this world
mcqs.why: The correct answer is complete faith in the life that is to come after this world. Hereafter means the life after death, and belief in it means having complete faith in that coming life.

mcqs.q: What is the translation of the verse وَبِالْآخِرَةِ هُمْ يُوقِنُونَ (Al-Baqarah: 4)?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is "They believe in the Hereafter." This verse, quoted in the book's exercise, shows the importance of belief in the Hereafter.

mcqs.q: Who taught the belief in the Hereafter?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is all the Prophets (AS). The book's own MCQ states that the belief in the Hereafter was taught by all the Prophets, not by any one Prophet alone.

mcqs.q: On the Day of Judgement, whose good and bad deeds will be weighed?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is of all human beings. The weighing of deeds on the Day of Judgement applies to every human being without exception.

mcqs.q: Belief in the Hereafter gives a person the sense of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is his own responsibility. This belief makes a person feel answerable for his deeds, as the book's exercise states.

mcqs.q: Faith in the Hereafter is the attribute of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the guided and successful people. The Quran presents belief in the Hereafter as a quality of those who are rightly guided and successful.

mcqs.q: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: The Hereafter life will be temporary
Paradise is the place of blessings and Hell is the place of punishment
Hell is the place of blessings
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that Paradise is the place of blessings and Hell is the place of punishment. The statement "Hell is the place of blessings" is incorrect, as corrected in the book's true/false exercise.

mcqs.q: The life of the Hereafter will be:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is eternal. The book's exercise corrects the false statement: the life of the Hereafter will be everlasting, not temporary.

mcqs.q: In the Hereafter, every person's deeds will be presented before:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the court of Allah Almighty. The fill-in exercise states that in the Hereafter every person's deeds will be presented before Allah's court.

mcqs.q: Those who are forgiven will enter:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Paradise. The book's exercise states that those who are forgiven will enter Paradise, the place of blessings.

mcqs.q: What will Allah Almighty do with this world and all its things?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that He will destroy them. The exercise states: Allah Almighty will destroy this world and all its things, after which the Hereafter will begin.

mcqs.q: Belief in the Hereafter makes a person:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is generous. The book's exercise says belief in the Hereafter makes a person generous, not miserly, because he hopes for reward from Allah.

mcqs.q: Belief in the Hereafter produces in a person:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is patience and tolerance. Facing the trials of life with the Hereafter in mind produces patience and tolerance, not anger.

mcqs.q: Every person will be questioned about:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is his responsibilities. The book's true/false exercise confirms: every person will be questioned about his responsibilities.

lessons.title: Fasting (Roza): Virtues and Social Effects
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning and Obligation of Fasting

  • The word used in Arabic for fasting (Roza) is "Sawm".
  • In Shariah, fasting means refraining from eating, drinking and physical desires from dawn until sunset, in order to gain the pleasure of Allah Almighty.
  • Fasting was made obligatory in 2 AH, in the month of Ramadan.
  • Fasting is obligatory on every sane, adult Muslim man and woman. Permission not to fast is given to the sick and to travellers.
  • Fasting is an important pillar of Islam.

Virtues of Fasting

  • The Holy Quran says: "O believers! Fasts have been made obligatory on you, as they were made obligatory on those before you, so that you may become righteous (God-fearing)."
  • The Holy Prophet ﷺ said: "The month of Ramadan is the month of compassion and sympathy."
  • According to the Hadith, by keeping the fasts of Ramadan, previous sins are forgiven.

Effects of Fasting

  • Fasting produces in a person self-control — the strength and ability to control oneself.
  • Fasting strengthens the idea of human equality, because rich and poor alike stay hungry and thirsty.
  • Fasting produces in a person the sense of Allah Almighty's sovereignty and of one's own humility and servitude.

mcqs.q: Which word is used in Arabic for fasting (Roza)?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Sawm. The book's exercise states that for fasting, the word used in Arabic is Sawm, not Sabr (patience).

mcqs.q: What is meant by keeping a fast in Shariah?
options: Refraining from eating, drinking and physical desires from dawn until sunset for Allah's pleasure
mcqs.why: The correct answer is refraining from eating, drinking and physical desires from dawn until sunset, in order to gain the pleasure of Allah Almighty — this is the Shariah definition given in the book.

mcqs.q: In which Hijri year was fasting made obligatory?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 2 AH. The book's exercise states clearly that fasting was made obligatory in 2 AH.

mcqs.q: On whom is fasting obligatory?
options: Every sane, adult Muslim man and woman
mcqs.why: The correct answer is every sane, adult Muslim man and woman. Fasting is not obligatory on children or on those who are not sane, as the book's MCQ confirms.

mcqs.q: Fasting is obligatory in the month of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Ramadan. The book corrects the false statement that fasts were made obligatory in Rajab — they were made obligatory in the month of Ramadan.

mcqs.q: Permission not to fast (with making up later) is given to:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the sick and travellers. The book's MCQ states that permission not to fast is given to the sick and to travellers.

mcqs.q: Complete the Quranic verse: "Fasts have been made obligatory on you, as they were made obligatory on those before you, so that you may become __________."
mcqs.why: The correct answer is righteous (God-fearing). The purpose of fasting given in the Quran is Taqwa — becoming righteous and God-fearing.

mcqs.q: The Holy Prophet ﷺ said: "The month of Ramadan is the month of __________ and sympathy."
mcqs.why: The correct answer is compassion. The Hadith quoted in the book calls Ramadan the month of compassion and sympathy, because people feel for the hungry and the poor in it.

mcqs.q: Fasting produces in a person __________ — the strength and ability to control oneself.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is self-control. The book's fill-in exercise states that fasting produces self-control in a person — the ability to control his desires.

mcqs.q: The time of fasting is from __________ until sunset.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is dawn. The book's exercise corrects the option: the time of fasting is from dawn, not sunrise, until sunset.

mcqs.q: According to the Hadith, by keeping the fasts of Ramadan, which sins are forgiven?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is previous sins. The book's exercise states that by keeping the fasts of Ramadan, a person's previous sins are forgiven.

mcqs.q: Which statement about fasting is correct?
options: Fasting strengthens the idea of human equality
Fasting is a minor act of worship
Fasting is obligatory on senseless people
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that fasting strengthens the idea of human equality. Rich and poor all remain hungry alike, and the statement about senseless people is false — fasting is obligatory on the sane and adult.

mcqs.q: Made obligatory in 2 AH:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is fasting. The book's MCQ asks this directly: fasting is the worship that was made obligatory in 2 AH.

mcqs.q: Fasting produces in a person the sense of:
options: Allah's sovereignty and his own humility and servitude
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Allah Almighty's sovereignty and one's own humility and servitude. The book's true/false exercise confirms this effect of fasting.

mcqs.q: Fasting is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that fasting is an important pillar of Islam. The book's exercise marks this statement correct — fasting is one of the fundamental pillars of Islam.

lessons.title: Hajj and Its Universal Status
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning of Hajj

  • The literal meaning of Hajj is "to intend and resolve".
  • In Shariah, Hajj means performing Tawaf of the House of Allah in Makkah on the appointed days of Hajj and completing the rites of Hajj at the other sacred places.
  • Hajj became obligatory in 9 AH.
  • Hajj is obligatory once in a lifetime on every sane, adult Muslim man and woman who has the means to reach the House of Allah.

Important Terms

TermMeaning
MiqatThe place where Ihram is put on
IhramMen wrapping two white sheets with the intention of Hajj (women remain in their own clothes)
TawafPerforming Tawaf (circling) of the Holy House of Allah
TalbiyahThe prayer recited after the intention of Hajj: "لَبَّيْكَ اللَّهُمَّ لَبَّيْكَ، لَبَّيْكَ لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ لَبَّيْكَ" — "Here I am, O Allah! Here I am; You have no partner"

Rites and Places

  • At Mina, the Jamarat are pelted with stones.
  • At Muzdalifah, the two prayers of Maghrib and Isha are offered together.
  • At Arafat, behind the Imam of Hajj, the two prayers of Zuhr and Asr are offered together.

Universal Status of Hajj

  • Hajj is a universal act of worship — the annual international gathering of Muslims takes place in Hajj.
  • Hajj is not only a financial act of worship; it is a combination of physical, financial and spiritual acts of worship (Jami-ul-Ibadat).
  • Hajj is an important means of expressing the unity and agreement of Muslims and human equality, and it teaches Muslims to sacrifice everything in the way of Allah.
  • Hajj also provides an opportunity for international trade and profit.
  • According to the Hadith, one who does not perform Hajj despite having the means will die as a Jew (i.e., outside the fold of obedience).

mcqs.q: What is the literal meaning of Hajj?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is "to intend and resolve." The book's exercise gives this as the literal meaning of Hajj, distinct from its Shariah meaning.

mcqs.q: What is meant by Hajj in Shariah?
options: Performing Tawaf of the House of Allah in Makkah on the appointed days and completing the rites at the sacred places
Fasting on the 9th of Zil Hajj
mcqs.why: The correct answer is performing Tawaf of the House of Allah in Makkah on the appointed days of Hajj and completing the rites of Hajj at the other sacred places — the book's Shariah definition.

mcqs.q: Hajj became obligatory in which year?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 9 AH. The book's fill-in exercise states that Hajj became obligatory in 9 AH.

mcqs.q: Hajj is obligatory in a lifetime:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is once. Hajj is obligatory only once in a lifetime, and only on the Muslim who has the means for it.

mcqs.q: What is meant by Miqat?
options: The place where Ihram is put on
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the place where Ihram is put on. The book's matching exercise defines Miqat in exactly these words.

mcqs.q: What is Ihram?
options: Men wrapping two white sheets with the intention of Hajj
mcqs.why: The correct answer is men wrapping two white sheets with the intention of Hajj, while women remain in their own clothes — as defined in the book's exercise.

mcqs.q: The prayer recited after the intention of Hajj, "Labbaik Allahumma Labbaik...", is called:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Talbiyah. The book defines Talbiyah as the prayer recited after the intention of Hajj: "Here I am, O Allah! Here I am; You have no partner."

mcqs.q: At which place are the Jamarat pelted with stones?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Mina. The book's fill-in exercise states that at the place of Mina, the Jamarat are pelted with stones.

mcqs.q: At which place are Maghrib and Isha prayers offered together during Hajj?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Muzdalifah. The book states that at Muzdalifah the two prayers of Maghrib and Isha are offered together.

mcqs.q: Behind the Imam of Hajj, Zuhr and Asr are offered together at:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Arafat. The book's MCQ states that at Arafat, behind the Imam of Hajj, Zuhr and Asr prayers are offered together.

mcqs.q: The annual international gathering of Muslims takes place in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Hajj. Muslims from all over the world gather at one place and time only in Hajj, making it the annual international gathering.

mcqs.q: Hajj is best described as:
options: Only a spiritual act of worship
Only a financial act of worship
Only a physical act of worship
A combination of physical, financial and spiritual acts of worship
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a combination of physical, financial and spiritual acts of worship. The book corrects the statement that Hajj is only financial — it is Jami-ul-Ibadat, the gatherer of all worships.

mcqs.q: Hajj is an important means of expressing:
options: The unity and agreement of Muslims and human equality
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the unity and agreement of Muslims and human equality. In identical dress, rich and poor stand together, and the book marks this statement correct.

mcqs.q: According to the Hadith, one who does not perform Hajj despite having the means will die as a:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a Jew. The book's exercise quotes this severe Hadith warning for the one who neglects Hajj despite having the means.

mcqs.q: Hajj teaches Muslims:
options: To sacrifice everything of theirs in the way of Allah

lessons.title: Khulq-e-Azeem (The Great Character)
lessons.notes_html:
Khulq-e-Azeem — The Highest Rank of Character

Khuluq-e-Azeem is the name of the highest rank of human character. In the Holy Quran, this attribute is described about the Noble Prophet Hazrat Muhammad Mustafa ﷺ: وَاِنَّكَ لَعَلٰى خُلُقٍ عَظِيۡمٍ (Al-Qalam: 4) — Translation: "Indeed, you are on a great (lofty) character." From the moral point of view, there was no such virtue that the Holy Prophet ﷺ did not possess.

Mercy for All the Worlds

  • Allah Almighty sent the Holy Prophet ﷺ as a mercy for all the worlds (Al-Anbiya: 107): "O Muhammad! We have sent you as a mercy for the worlds."
  • Believers, disbelievers, hypocrites, women, children, slaves and even animals — all benefited from the boundless mercy and compassion of the Holy Prophet ﷺ.
  • The Holy Prophet ﷺ also treated animals with mercy and compassion, and he forbade making animals fight one another.

Mercy and Kindness in Practice

  • Once, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ kissed Hazrat Hasan (RA). Aqra bin Habis (RA) said: "I have ten children, but I have never kissed any of them." The Holy Prophet ﷺ replied in the words of the lesson: the person who does not show mercy will not be shown mercy.
  • "The one who does not show compassion to the young is not among us."
  • The Holy Prophet ﷺ said: "The best among you are those who are best to their family members."
  • For the one who gives the call to religion, it is extremely necessary to be of excellent character.

options: The Noble Prophet Hazrat Muhammad Mustafa ﷺ
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Noble Prophet Hazrat Muhammad Mustafa ﷺ. The Quran says: "Indeed, you are on a great (lofty) character" (Al-Qalam: 4), addressing the Prophet ﷺ.

Indeed, you are a great king

mcqs.why: The correct answer is "Indeed, you are on a great (lofty) character." This is the translation given in the book's own exercise for Al-Qalam: 4.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is that all benefited — believers, disbelievers, hypocrites, women, children, slaves and even animals — from the boundless mercy of the Holy Prophet ﷺ, as the book's long answer states.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is the young. The book's sentence-completion exercise gives this saying of the Holy Prophet ﷺ about compassion to the young.

lessons.title: Sabr and Tahammul (Patience and Tolerance)
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning of Sabr and Tahammul

  • The literal meaning of Sabr is to keep oneself under control; the literal meaning of Tahammul is to bear a burden.
  • In the terminology of Shariah, Sabr and Tahammul mean bearing the pains and difficulties that come in life with patience and remaining calm, and bearing, for the sake of Allah's pleasure, the pains and troubles that come while striving for the glory of Allah Almighty's religion.
  • One type of Sabr is to bear the pains and difficulties of life and remain calm, without wailing, lamentation or impatience.

Reward of the Patient

  • اِنَّمَا يُوَفَّى الصّٰبِرُوۡنَ اَجۡرَهُمۡ بِغَيۡرِ حِسَابٍ (Az-Zumar: 10) — Meaning: "Only the patient will be given their reward without measure (without reckoning)."
  • Indeed, Allah Almighty is with the patient.
  • With Sabr and Tahammul, difficulties become easy, and by practising them reward is earned.

The Example of the Holy Prophet ﷺ

  • The Messenger of Allah ﷺ showed great Sabr and Tahammul in his Makkan life. From his excellent example (Uswah Hasanah) we learn that for achieving a great objective, Sabr and Tahammul are necessary.
  • The people of Taif stoned the Holy Prophet ﷺ and covered him in blood; even then, he prayed for them: "O Allah! Guide them."
  • In Makkah, Hazrat Yasir (RA) and his wife Hazrat Bibi Sumayya (RA) were martyred with extreme cruelty for embracing faith.
  • Through the brief struggle of twenty-three years of the Holy Prophet ﷺ, the light of Tawhid began to shine throughout the Arabian Peninsula.

options: Bearing the pains and difficulties of life with patience and remaining calm
mcqs.why: The correct answer is bearing the pains and difficulties that come in life with patience and remaining calm. The book corrects the opposite statement as false and gives this as the Shariah meaning.

options: The patient will be tested again

mcqs.why: The correct answer is "Only the patient will be given their reward without measure (without reckoning)." This is the meaning of the verse as given in the book's exercise.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is to keep oneself under control. The book's matching exercise gives this as the literal meaning of Sabr.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is the patient. The book's MCQ and matching exercise both state: Allah Almighty is with the patient.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is that they covered him in blood. The book's MCQ records the cruelty of Taif, where the Prophet ﷺ was stoned until he bled.

options: O Allah! Make them fight among themselves

mcqs.why: The correct answer is "O Allah! Guide them." Instead of cursing them, the Prophet ﷺ prayed for their guidance — the supreme example of Sabr and Tahammul in the book's MCQ.

options: Hazrat Yasir (RA) and Hazrat Bibi Sumayya (RA)
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Hazrat Yasir (RA) and his wife Hazrat Bibi Sumayya (RA). The book's long answer states they were martyred in Makkah with extreme cruelty for embracing faith, and corrects the claim about Hazrat Hamza (RA).

mcqs.why: The correct answer is Sabr and Tahammul. The book's fill-in exercise draws this lesson from the excellent example of the Holy Prophet ﷺ.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is Tahammul. The book's fill-in exercise states: with Sabr and Tahammul, difficulties become easy.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is twenty-three years. The book's fill-in exercise calls it his brief struggle of twenty-three years, through which Tawhid spread across the Arabian Peninsula.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is Sabr and Tahammul. The book corrects the false statement that it is called Shukr; bearing such pains for Allah's pleasure is Sabr and Tahammul.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is to bear the pains and difficulties of life and remain calm, without expressing wailing, lamentation or impatience — the type of Sabr described in the book's long answer.

lessons.title: Ikhlas and Taqwa (Sincerity and God-consciousness)
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning of Ikhlas

  • The literal meaning of Ikhlas is to purify. The word "Khalis" is used for something that is free from adulteration.
  • In religion, Ikhlas means that whatever a person does, he does purely to gain the pleasure of Allah Almighty, without mixing any personal benefit or motive with it.
  • One who works with Ikhlas is called Mukhlis (sincere).
  • The accepted deed is the one which is done purely to gain the pleasure and approval of Allah Almighty.

The Hadith on Intentions

  • The Holy Prophet ﷺ said: اِنَّمَا الْاَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ — "The reward of deeds depends on intentions"; that is, only the deed performed with a sincere intention for the pleasure of Allah Almighty is accepted.
  • Deeds depend on intentions, and the worth and value of deeds depends on sincere intention.
  • Allah Almighty does not look at your faces and wealth, but at your hearts and deeds.

Meaning of Taqwa

  • The literal meaning of Taqwa is to save, to protect, to abstain.
  • In Shariah, Taqwa means purity of heart, sincerity of intention, and the growth of Allah Almighty's love and fear in the heart.
  • فَمَنِ اتَّقٰى وَاَصۡلَحَ فَلَا خَوۡفٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَلَا هُمۡ يَحۡزَنُوۡنَ (Al-Araf: 35) — "Those who fear (Allah) and reform themselves will have no fear, nor will they grieve."
  • Greatness and nobility is the name of Taqwa; Islam declared Taqwa to be the standard of excellence. No Arab has superiority over a non-Arab, and no non-Arab over an Arab — superiority is only by Taqwa.
  • The summary and real purpose of Islamic injunctions — faith, Salah, fasting, Hajj, sacrifice — is only Taqwa.
  • Allah divided mankind into tribes and nations so that they may recognise one another.

Doing deeds to be seen by people
mcqs.why: The correct answer is doing whatever one does purely to gain the pleasure of Allah Almighty, without mixing any personal benefit or motive — the book's definition of Ikhlas.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is to purify. The book's completion exercise states the literal meaning of Ikhlas is to purify, and "Khalis" is used for something free from adulteration.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is to save, to protect, to abstain. The book's completion exercise gives this literal meaning of Taqwa.

lessons.title: Adl and Ihsan (Justice and Benevolence)
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning of Adl

  • The literal meaning of Adl is to divide something into two equal parts; Adl is an Arabic word.
  • Adl means that one who does good should be treated with good, and if someone does evil, an equal recompense should be taken from him; that is, doing every task on time and putting everything in its proper place is called "Adl".
  • In reality, Adl is the attribute of Allah Almighty, on which the universe is based. Through Adl, justice is achieved.
  • اِعۡدِلُوۡا هُوَ اَقۡرَبُ لِلتَّقۡوٰى — "Do justice, for it is nearer to Taqwa." In this verse the command is of Adl.

Meaning of Ihsan

  • Ihsan means taking the initiative in doing good, returning good for good and returning good even for evil; Ihsan is also that every task should be performed in a beautiful and excellent manner — creating beauty in every task is Ihsan.
  • اِنَّ اللّٰهَ يَاۡمُرُ بِالۡعَدۡلِ وَالۡاِحۡسَانِ (An-Nahl: 90) — Meaning: "Indeed, Allah (Almighty) commands justice and benevolence (doing Ihsan)."
  • Adl is the name of law, whereas Ihsan is the name of character.

Conduct of the Holy Prophet ﷺ

  • When someone filed a case against another in the court of the Holy Prophet ﷺ, he would give a just decision — in his court there was no distinction between one's own and strangers, Muslim and non-Muslim, strong and weak.
  • But if someone behaved improperly towards him personally, he would not take revenge for himself; rather, showing Ihsan, he would forgive and pray for that person's guidance.
  • Thus the Holy Prophet ﷺ showed Adl in national (public) matters and Ihsan in personal matters, and taught: forgive one another's shortcomings and faults.

mcqs.q: What is meant by Adl (justice)?
options: Doing every task on time and putting everything in its proper place; good for good and equal recompense for evil
mcqs.why: The correct answer is doing every task on time and putting everything in its proper place, treating good with good and taking equal recompense for evil — the book's definition of Adl.

mcqs.q: What is meant by Ihsan (benevolence)?
options: Taking the initiative in doing good, returning good for good and good even for evil, and doing every task beautifully
mcqs.why: The correct answer is taking the initiative in doing good, returning good for good and returning good even for evil. The book's MCQ confirms this is called Ihsan, not Adl.

mcqs.q: What is the meaning of اِنَّ اللّٰهَ يَاۡمُرُ بِالۡعَدۡلِ وَالۡاِحۡسَانِ (An-Nahl: 90)?
options: Indeed, Allah commands justice and benevolence
mcqs.why: The correct answer is "Indeed, Allah (Almighty) commands justice and benevolence (doing Ihsan)." This is the meaning of the verse given in the book's exercise.

options: To divide something into two equal parts
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to divide something into two equal parts. The book's matching exercise gives this as the literal meaning of Adl.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is Adl. The book's MCQ states that this verse commands justice, and adds: "Do justice, for it is nearer to Taqwa."

mcqs.why: The correct answer is Arabic. The book's MCQ states that Adl is a word of the Arabic language.

mcqs.q: Through Adl is achieved:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is justice. The book's MCQ states that through Adl, justice is achieved in society.

mcqs.q: Taking initiative in good, returning good for evil and more good for good is called:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Ihsan. The book's MCQ gives exactly this description and names it Ihsan.

mcqs.q: In the court of the Holy Prophet ﷺ, distinction was made between:
options: No one — there was no distinction between own and stranger, Muslim and non-Muslim, strong and weak
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that there was no distinction at all. The book's true/false exercise confirms that in his court there was no distinction between one's own and strangers, Muslim and non-Muslim, strong and weak.

mcqs.q: Creating beauty in every task is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Ihsan. The book corrects the statement "creating beauty in every task is also Adl" — it is Ihsan, doing every task in a beautiful and excellent manner.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is law / character. The book corrects the reversed statement: Adl is the name of law, whereas Ihsan is the name of character.

options: Not take revenge; instead forgive and pray for the person's guidance
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that he would not take revenge for himself; rather, showing Ihsan, he would forgive and pray for that person's guidance — as the book's long answer describes.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is case. The book's fill-in exercise states that when someone filed a case in his court against another, he would do justice.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is Allah Almighty. The book's fill-in exercise states that Adl is in reality the attribute of Allah Almighty, on which the universe is based.

lessons.title: Husn-e-Muashrat (Good Social Conduct)
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning of Husn-e-Muashrat

Man is a social creature; he cannot live alone, but lives together with others in society. Whatever society a person lives in, his relations are established with the people there. To maintain those relations in a good manner is called "Husn-e-Muashrat". It means that everyone should be given his due, good relations should be kept with one's whole environment and all its members, they should be treated well, elders should be respected and the young treated with compassion, and every person should be honoured according to his rank and position.

Quranic Command (An-Nisa: 36)

Allah Almighty has commanded, along with His worship, good conduct with parents, relatives, orphans, the poor, near and far neighbours, companions, travellers and one's subordinates: "Worship Allah Almighty and treat parents, relatives, orphans, the poor, near and far neighbours, companions, travellers and one's subordinates well."

Teachings of the Holy Prophet ﷺ

  • "Whoever breaks ties with you, join ties with him; whoever wrongs you, forgive him; and whoever does evil to you, do good to him."
  • "Greet every person, whether you know him or not."
  • Whoever wrongs you, you should forgive him and let go. No one's thing should be taken without his permission. If someone gives you something or offers you something to drink, you must express his thanks.
  • Islam also guides us: do not spoil anyone's name.

Conduct of the Holy Prophet ﷺ

  • The Holy Prophet ﷺ treated his near ones, relatives, friends, neighbours, young and old, all well, and helped them physically, financially and morally. If someone fell ill, he would go to visit him.
  • When famine struck Makkah, a representative of its people came to Madinah and requested help; the Holy Prophet ﷺ arranged gold coins (ashrafis) and grain for him and prayed for the famine to end.
  • He continued dealings and good conduct even with the Jews, despite their opposition; and if a person came to him, he would meet him with a smiling face.
  • Husn-e-Muashrat includes participating in people's weddings and sorrows, caring for the disabled, the sick, the elderly and women, and not disturbing people's rest with loud radio, TV or loudspeaker.
  • That person will earn the rank of the worst person before Allah Almighty whose misconduct makes people stop meeting him. In the Quran and Sunnah, the basis of honour and dignity has been declared to be good morals and good character.

mcqs.q: Maintaining social relations in a good manner is called:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Husn-e-Muashrat. The book's MCQ gives this exact definition: maintaining social relations in a good manner is Husn-e-Muashrat.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is treating one another well and maintaining relations in a good manner. The book corrects the statement that it means quarrelling — Husn-e-Muashrat is good treatment of everyone.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is parents, relatives, orphans, the poor, near and far neighbours, companions, travellers and one's subordinates. The book's long answer lists all of these from An-Nisa: 36.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is greet him. The book's MCQ quotes the Hadith: greet every person, whether you know him or not.

mcqs.q: Complete the Hadith: "Whoever breaks ties with you, join ties with him; whoever wrongs you, ______ him."
mcqs.why: The correct answer is forgive him. The book's long answer and fill-in exercise both complete the teaching in this way: whoever wrongs you, forgive him and let go.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is permission. The book's fill-in exercise states: no one's thing should be taken without his permission.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is thanks. The book's fill-in exercise teaches that gratitude must be expressed to the one who gives or offers something.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is ashrafis (gold coins) — and grain. The book's MCQ and long answer record that he arranged gold coins and grain for the famine-stricken people of Makkah and prayed for the famine to end.

lessons.title: The Style of Conversation of Hazrat Muhammad ﷺ
lessons.notes_html:
Points of the Prophet's ﷺ Style of Conversation

  • When the Holy Prophet ﷺ wanted to impress the importance of something, he would repeat it again and again.
  • According to the occasion, he would adopt sharpness and softness in voice and tone, and he would move his hands as needed.
  • To attract people's attention, he would sometimes ask a question, and sometimes repeat that question again and again so that people would become fully attentive.
  • He would not make his talk so long that people would get tired; in a short time he would speak briefly but comprehensively.
  • While speaking, he would pronounce words slowly, in such a manner that the listeners could easily memorise them; the words were neither fewer nor more than needed.
  • Generally, during conversation, a smile remained on his blessed face. Hazrat Abdullah bin Harith (RA) says: "I never saw anyone smiling more than the Holy Prophet ﷺ."

Quranic Guidance

Allah Almighty says: قُل لَّهُمْ فِي أَنفُسِهِمْ قَوْلًا بَلِيغًا (An-Nisa: 63) — Translation: "And say to them words that reach their hearts." That is, conversation should be such that it reaches the listener's heart and affects it. The speaking style of Hazrat Muhammad ﷺ was such that the talk would reach the depths of the heart.

Teaching through Examples

  • The Holy Prophet ﷺ would explain a point with wisdom or by giving an example, so that the point may be well understood and fully remembered.
  • Example of the five prayers: he asked that if a canal flowed in front of someone's house and he bathed in it five times a day, would any dirt remain on his body? The Companions replied: "No dirt at all." He said: "Exactly the same is the example of the five prayers; Allah Almighty erases sins through them."
  • Once he drew a straight line and, besides it, some crooked lines, and explained that the straight line is Sirat-e-Mustaqeem, the straight path of safety, and the crooked lines are the paths of misguidance — Islam alone is the one straight path.

Guidance for Us

From the Seerah and style of conversation of the Holy Prophet ﷺ we get the guidance that our character, conduct and conversation should also follow his way, so that feelings of love and respect for us awaken in people and they listen to our talk with attention and interest; then our advice will not go in vain.

lessons.title: Domestic Life (Gharelu Zindagi)
lessons.notes_html:
The Command about Family Members

  • The Holy Prophet ﷺ said: "The best among you is the one who treats his family members well, and I am the best among you in treating family members well."
  • In another narration: "A perfect believer is the one who is excellent in morals and most kind to his family members." Good morals and good conduct with family members were declared the sign of the perfection of faith.
  • The standard of a person being good or bad is what his conduct with family members is.
  • The blessed life of the Noble Prophet ﷺ is the best Uswah Hasanah (excellent example) for us and worthy of being followed.

Domestic Routines of the Holy Prophet ﷺ

  • Hazrat Aisha (RA) was asked what the Holy Prophet ﷺ used to do when he came home. She said: He would look after his clothes, milk the goat, and fulfil his needs himself.
  • He would himself stitch his clothes and blessed shoes, cut wood, feed fodder to the animals, and meet family members with good speech and a smiling, open face.
  • When he entered the house or left the house, he would greet the family members with Salam.
  • His gentle temperament was such that, let alone scolding any servant or family member, he never even scolded (in anger).

Guidance of Women and Journeys

  • The Noble Prophet ﷺ would instruct his family members to learn religious matters, act on them and convey them to others.
  • Through the Azwaj-e-Mutahharat (pure wives), he would guide common women in religious matters; women would learn about their issues through the Azwaj-e-Mutahharat.
  • When he intended to go on a journey, he would cast lots among the names of the Azwaj-e-Mutahharat; the wife whose name came out in the lot, he would take her along.
  • His son Hazrat Ibrahim (RA) was kept in a house in Madinah for foster-nursing (Razaat).
  • He said: "Live life as a traveller lives" — that is, without attachment to the world.

lessons.title: Amr bil Maroof wa Nahi anil Munkar (Commanding Good and Forbidding Evil)
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning

  • The literal meaning of "Amr" is to command something, and the literal meaning of "Nahi" is to forbid something.
  • In terminology, every good deed that Allah and His Messenger commanded to be done is "Maroof", and every evil deed that Allah and His Messenger forbade is "Munkar". Therefore, Amr bil Maroof and Nahi anil Munkar means "to command good and to forbid evil".
  • For this work, the words "Dawat" and "Tabligh" are also used.

Importance

  • The religion that began with Hazrat Adam (AS) was completed through the last Prophet Hazrat Muhammad ﷺ; now no new Prophet will come until the Day of Judgement. Therefore, after the Holy Prophet ﷺ, this duty has been collectively made obligatory on the Muslim Ummah.
  • وَلْتَكُن مِّنكُمْ أُمَّةٌ يَدْعُونَ إِلَى الْخَيْرِ وَيَأْمُرُونَ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَيَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ الْمُنكَرِ (Aal-e-Imran: 104) — "And there should be among you a group that calls towards good, commands good deeds and forbids evil deeds."
  • كُنتُمْ خَيْرَ أُمَّةٍ أُخْرِجَتْ لِلنَّاسِ تَأْمُرُونَ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَتَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ الْمُنكَرِ (Aal-e-Imran: 110) — "You are the best Ummah raised for the people; you command good deeds and forbid evil deeds."
  • On the occasion of Hajjat-ul-Wida, the Holy Prophet ﷺ said: those who are present here should convey my message to the absent.

Principles and Rules

  • Being practical: the caller must first act on the good himself. أَتَأْمُرُونَ النَّاسَ بِالْبِرِّ وَتَنسَوْنَ أَنفُسَكُمْ (Al-Baqarah: 44) — "Do you command people to do good and forget yourselves, while you read the Book?"
  • Beginning from one's own home: وَأَنذِرْ عَشِيرَتَكَ الْأَقْرَبِينَ (Ash-Shuara: 214) — "And warn your nearest relatives"; and يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا قُوا أَنفُسَكُمْ وَأَهْلِيكُمْ نَارًا (At-Tahrim: 6) — "O believers! Save yourselves and your families from the Fire whose fuel will be people and stones."
  • Wisdom and good advice: ادْعُ إِلَىٰ سَبِيلِ رَبِّكَ بِالْحِكْمَةِ وَالْمَوْعِظَةِ الْحَسَنَةِ (An-Nahl: 125) — "Invite people to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good advice." Speak to people according to their understanding; extreme harshness should not be used.
  • According to one's capacity: the Holy Prophet ﷺ said: "If any one of you sees an evil, he should stop it with his hand; if he cannot, he should stop it with his tongue; if he cannot do even that, he should consider it bad in his heart — and that is the weakest degree of faith." Stopping evil by hand is the work of the government and rulers; by tongue, of the common person.

lessons.title: Halal Kamai (Halal Earning)
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning of Halal Earning

  • The literal meaning of "Halal" is lawful and correct.
  • Halal earning means that lawful and correct earning which is earned in a way that Shariah has declared lawful and correct.
  • Allah Almighty commands His servants to earn livelihood by lawful means and to use Halal and pure things, and forbids earning by unlawful means.
  • The Holy Prophet ﷺ said: طَلَبُ كَسْبِ الْحَلَالِ فَرِيضَةٌ بَعْدَ الْفَرِيضَةِ — "Seeking Halal livelihood is an important obligation after the obligatory acts of worship."
  • فَإِذَا قُضِيَتِ الصَّلَاةُ فَانْتَشِرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَابْتَغُوا مِنْ فَضْلِ اللَّهِ (Al-Jumuah: 10) — "Then when the Salah is completed, disperse in the land and seek Allah's bounty (livelihood)."

Halal Sources of Income

  • Trading according to Shariah principles, farming, craftsmanship and artistry, hunting Halal animals, employment and labour, etc.

Haram Sources of Income

  • Trading against the principles of Shariah, drugs, the business of interest (usury), gambling, theft, robbery, hunting Haram animals, lottery, and earning obtained by deceiving someone, adulterating goods, hoarding, giving bribes, or through oppression and force.
  • If a person adopts an unlawful method, evidently its harm will fall on other people.
  • One who earns through Haram sources does not attain the pleasure of Allah Almighty.

Effects of Halal Earning

  • All the Prophets (AS) taught the lesson of Halal earning through word and deed, and emphasised it.
  • "Keep your food and drink Halal, then every prayer (dua) of yours will be accepted." The prayer of one who eats Halal livelihood is accepted, and children brought up on Halal earning become righteous.

lessons.title: Honesty in Business (Karobar mein Dayanatdari)
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning of Honesty in Business

Honesty in business means that truthfulness and trustworthiness should be observed in dealings and trade, pure goods should be given, nothing should be given by hiding its defect, weighing and measuring instruments should be kept correct and honest, and every kind of fraud should be avoided. Selling adulterated and health-harming goods is business dishonesty.

Importance of Honesty in Business

  • Islam has given great importance to honesty in business. The honest trader will be with the Prophets, the truthful and the martyrs.
  • For the businessman who trades with truthfulness and honesty, good news of blessing in wealth and business in this world has been given.
  • Business depends on trust: the person who does not practise fraud and dishonesty gains the strong trust of customers, and his business grows.
  • The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "One who has no honesty has no faith either." Honesty in business is a matter of faith.
  • "The person who practises fraud in business is not among us."
  • A person who is dishonest in business cannot attain popularity with Allah and people; the dishonest person faces Allah Almighty's severe anger and lack of blessing in this world.

Warning for Short Weight and Measure

  • In Surah Al-Mutaffifin, those who give short weight and measure — that is, those who are dishonest in measuring and weighing — have been declared deserving of Allah Almighty's punishment: وَيْلٌ لِلْمُطَفِّفِينَ — "Woe (destruction) for those who give short weight and measure."

Honest Traders Spread Islam

  • In the early period of Islam, the message of Islam reached many far-off regions through honest Muslim traders; Islam reached Malaysia, Indonesia and China through such honest traders.
  • Note in the book: honesty in business by non-Muslims is only their cleverness (worldly wisdom), whereas for a Muslim it is a matter of faith.
  • The greatest share in all the progress seen in the world today is of trade.

lessons.title: Discipline and Respect for Law (Nazm-o-Zabt aur Qanoon ka Ehtram)
lessons.notes_html:
Meanings

  • Discipline (Nazm-o-Zabt) means abiding by laws and principles (rules).
  • The principles and rules made for running any country are called law.
  • Respect for law means that the law should be obeyed; by following the law, every citizen gets his right, the country runs with full order, and peace and tranquillity remain established in society.
  • Obeying the law is every citizen's duty and responsibility; it is the responsibility of a good citizen to respect the laws of the country.

Lesson of Discipline from the Universe and Worship

  • The entire system of the universe runs under discipline. The verse of Surah Yaseen (38-40) gives the example: "The sun moves towards its appointed place" and stages are fixed for the moon — this teaches us the lesson of discipline.
  • The worship system of Islam also teaches us the lesson of discipline: offering Salah at fixed times, fasting in a specific month, Sehri and Iftar at fixed times, and Hajj at a fixed time — all make us bound to discipline.
  • If we individually demonstrate discipline, then collective discipline will be created.
  • By acting on the law, discipline will be created in the country.

The Example of the Holy Prophet ﷺ

  • Regarding the enforcement of law, the Noble Prophet ﷺ made no distinction between young and old, rich and poor, white and black; enforcement of law should be equal for all.
  • The Holy Prophet ﷺ said: "If anyone has any right due from me, let him come and take it from me."
  • For a student, observing discipline is very important, and it is necessary for every person to observe discipline within his own limits.

lessons.title: Milli Ittehad (National Unity)
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning of Milli Ittehad

  • The becoming one of a nation under a belief, ideology, action and purpose is called "Milli Ittehad", that is, "national unity".
  • Ideological uniformity binds Muslims in a strong bond of Milli Ittehad. The source of guidance for all human beings is the Holy Quran, and the social life of all Muslims is uniformity.
  • Our strength, progress and prosperity depend entirely on our Milli Ittehad. In unity there is blessing, whereas in disunity and discord there is lack of blessing.
  • All Muslims are among themselves like one body. "A Muslim is one from whose hand and tongue other Muslims are safe."
  • Apart from Islam, the followers of all other religions and ideologies have all been declared separate "Millats".

Quranic Teachings

  • "And remember Allah's blessing on you when you were enemies of one another; then He put affection in your hearts, and by His grace you became brothers of one another." (Aal-e-Imran: 103)
  • "And all together hold fast to the rope of Allah and do not split up."
  • "Establish the religion and do not split up in it."
  • "Do not differ, lest you become weak and your strength departs."
  • The saying of the Prophet ﷺ is: "O servants of Allah! Become friends of one another."

Historical Points

  • Before Islam, Arab tribes used to fight among themselves over small matters; their seven hundred battles among themselves are famous.
  • Through their Milli Ittehad, the Muslims gained control over a large part of the world.
  • Through Zakat, Muslims help one another financially — one of the practical bonds of unity.

lessons.title: Huqooq-ul-Ibad (Rights of Orphans, Widows, the Disabled and Travellers)
lessons.notes_html:
Key Definitions

TermMeaning
Orphan (Yateem)Every minor child whose father has passed away
Widow (Bewah)The woman whose husband has passed away
Disabled (Mazoor)Those people who, due to physical or mental weakness, or the loss of an organ, cannot fully carry out the necessities and tasks of their life
Traveller (Musafir)Every person who has gone far from his home and family for work, due to some compulsion or need
Huqooq AllahOur responsibilities made obligatory on us by Allah Almighty — e.g. Tawhid, fulfilment of obligatory duties, obedience to the commands
Huqooq-ul-IbadThose responsibilities imposed by Allah Almighty on servants for one another; it is the duty of one servant to fulfil the right of another

Rights of Orphans and Widows

  • Islam commands us to keep the orphan's wealth separate from our own wealth (not mixed).
  • The best house among houses is the one in which an orphan is treated with gentleness (treated well).
  • In the presence of children, a widow will get from her husband's property a one-eighth share; if a widow has no children, she will get a fourth share.
  • The people most deserving of our sympathy and cooperation are those who suffer from some disability.

Rights of the Disabled and Travellers

  • Guiding a blind or lame person is also charity (Sadaqah).
  • Allah Almighty says in the Holy Quran: "And give relatives, the poor and travellers their due."
  • Companions and travellers should be treated with good conduct and kindness: "Treat those sitting around and fellow travellers with kindness."
  • Instead of taking service from a fellow traveller, serving him should be preferred.
  • When parting from a Muslim, give him some gift and bid him farewell with prayers: "I entrust your religion, trust and the end of your deeds to Allah Almighty."
  • The person who removes a hardship of his Muslim brother — on the Day of Judgement Allah Almighty will remove one of his hardships.

lessons.title: Hazrat Fatimah Az-Zahra (RA)
lessons.notes_html:
Birth and Family

  • According to the authentic narration, Hazrat Fatimah Az-Zahra (RA) was born in Makkah five years before Prophethood, when the Holy Prophet ﷺ was 35 years old and her noble mother, Hazrat Khadijah Al-Kubra (RA), was 50 years old.
  • Among the children of Hazrat Bibi Khadijah Al-Kubra (RA), Hazrat Fatimah Batool (RA) was the youngest.
  • Her titles include "Sayyidah Nisa Ahl Al-Jannah" (Leader of the women of Paradise), "Zahra", "Batool" and "Tahirah". The meaning of "Batool" is one who cuts off ties with the world (devoting herself to Allah).
  • The Holy Prophet ﷺ said: "Fatimah (RA) is a piece of my liver (heart)."

Marriage and Children

  • Her husband was Hazrat Ali (AS) (Hazrat Ali Karram Allahu Wajhahu). The marriage took place in 2 AH with great simplicity; Hazrat Ali (AS) had a horse and an armour — he sold the armour and arranged the marriage.
  • The dower (Haq Mehr) of Hazrat Fatimah Az-Zahra (RA) was fixed at four hundred dirhams.
  • She had six children: Hazrat Imam Hasan (RA), Hazrat Imam Husain (RA), Hazrat Muhsin (RA), Hazrat Umm Kulthum (RA), Hazrat Ruqayya (RA) and Hazrat Zainab (RA).
  • Allah Almighty kept the progeny of the Holy Prophet ﷺ alive through the children of Hazrat Fatimah Az-Zahra (RA). (Note: Hazrat Khadijah Al-Kubra (RA) was the grandmother of Hasan and Husain (RA); their mother was Hazrat Fatimah (RA).)
  • Once the Noble Prophet ﷺ set aside food and some money and said: send this share to Hazrat Fatimah Az-Zahra (RA).

Character

  • Although Hazrat Fatimah (RA) was herself hungry, she never sent a beggar (one who asks) back empty-handed.
  • In the Battle of Uhud, Hazrat Fatimah (RA) burned her mat and applied its ash to the wounds of the Holy Prophet ﷺ.
  • Her age at the time of her death was about 29 years.

lessons.title: Muhammad bin Qasim (RA)
lessons.notes_html:
Early Life

  • Muhammad bin Qasim was born in Taif in 75 AH, corresponding to 694 CE.
  • At the age of 14, he sought to join the army of Damascus, and after gaining expertise and ability in military training, he was appointed to a high military post.
  • Hajjaj bin Yusuf gave him an army of 6000, with 5 catapults (manjaniq).

Cause of the Conquest of Sindh

  • The immediate cause: several widows and orphan children of Muslim traders settled on the island of Serendip were travelling by ship towards Kufa when, due to opposing winds, the ship anchored at the port of Debal in Sindh; the ruler's men there looted the Muslim passengers and imprisoned the men, women and children. This became the cause of the attack on Sindh.
  • The siege of Debal city continued for six months. According to Hajjaj bin Yusuf's guidance, the catapult was placed in a specific direction and stones were hurled at the city; Muhammad bin Qasim specially targeted the central dome of the city, because as long as that dome remained safe, the morale of the townspeople would remain high.

Victory over Raja Dahir

  • The battle between Muhammad bin Qasim and Raja Dahir took place near the Aror fort. At that time, the number of Muhammad bin Qasim's army was fifteen thousand. Raja Dahir, while fighting, was riding on an elephant.
  • On 10 Ramadan 93 AH, Muhammad bin Qasim defeated Raja Dahir of Sindh.
  • Sindh got the title of "Bab-ul-Islam" (Gateway of Islam).

His Government

  • The government that Muhammad bin Qasim established over Sindh was itself an example in peace, order and justice.
  • He treated the people of Sindh with tolerance and gave them religious freedom. (Note in the book: the followers of Buddhism were in Debal, who supported Muhammad bin Qasim; the book does not mention that Raja Dahir belonged to Buddhism.)

lessons.title: Abu Ali Ibn Sina (RA)
lessons.notes_html:
Birth and Early Fame

  • Abu Ali Ibn Sina was born in "Afshana", a village of Bukhara, in 370 AH, corresponding to 980 CE.
  • He was a famous physician of the Islamic world and a famous scientist. At only twelve (12) years of age, he began to be called "Haziq Hakeem" (skilled physician).
  • His title was "Al-Sheikh Al-Rais" (not "Muallim-e-Awwal").
  • He was appointed to the post of minister twice.

His Famous Books

  • His more famous books are "Al-Qanun fi Al-Tibb" (The Canon of Medicine) and "Kitab Al-Shifa".
  • "Al-Qanun fi Al-Tibb" consists of five volumes. It remained part of the curriculum in the medical colleges of Europe for centuries; it was published sixteen times in the fifteenth century and twenty times in the sixteenth century, and was also translated into Latin and French.
  • The Europeans valued the scholarly achievements of Ibn Sina greatly; they translated his books into their own languages and benefited greatly from them.

His Views

  • He was the first to include psychology (Ilm Al-Nafs) in medicine. His view was that human emotions and feelings — happiness, grief, anger, worry — are connected with the heart, and are deeply connected with the circulation of blood and other fluids; enmity, cowardice and miserliness can be controlled by medical methods.
  • His view was that mercury, silver or any metal cannot be converted into gold through a chemical process.

Character and Last Years

  • Ibn Sina was a person of high character and good morals, a dignified and contented personality. When he felt sleepy during night study, he would eat and drink something (to refresh himself).
  • In his last years, he remained engaged in the recitation of the Quran.
  • He suffered from stomach ache (the disease from which he suffered) and passed away in 1037 CE.

lessons.title: Shah Waliullah Muhaddis Dehlavi (RA)
lessons.notes_html:
Birth and Era

  • Shah Waliullah (RA) was born on 4 Shawwal 1114 AH, corresponding to 10 February 1703 CE. His name was Qutbuddin Ahmad and "Waliullah" was his title.
  • His father's name was Shah Abdul Rahim.
  • In the era in which he opened his eyes, the Muslims of the subcontinent had become victims of decline in mental, intellectual, religious, economic and political terms, and the nation had reached the last edge of destruction.

Education and Services

  • At only 15 years of age, he completed his education at Madrasah Rahimiyah, established by his father.
  • He travelled to the holy Hijaz in around 1731 CE for higher education and to perform Hajj, and studied under famous scholars there, like Sheikh Abu Tahir Madani, Wand Allah Makki and Tajuddin Qalai.
  • In 1733 CE he returned to Delhi and, at the age of 30 years, took over the management of Madrasah Rahimiyah, along with research, writing, compilation and teaching.
  • Shah Waliullah felt that due to distance from the teaching of the Holy Quran, differences among the Muslims were increasing; he made full efforts for the second rising (Nashaat-e-Saniya) of the Muslims.
  • He clarified that sovereignty is reserved only for the being of Allah Almighty, and he drew the attention of the Muslims towards Ijtihad and research (Tahqeeq).

His Writings

  • His Persian translation of the Holy Quran is named "Fath-ur-Rahman".
  • The treatise he wrote to remove (end) the juristic differences of the Muslims was named "Al-Insaf fi Bayan Sabab Al-Ikhtilaf".

Death

  • He passed away on 29 Muharram 1179 AH, corresponding to 20 August 1762 CE, at the age of 61 years.
